name: Question 16
problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(-4,{\sigma }^{2})$ is a normal random variable with $P(-18<X<10)=0.1113,$ find  $\sigma .$

| $z$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.0\,$ | $\,0.5080\,$ | $\,0.5120\,$ | $\,0.5160\,$ |
| $\,0.1\,$ | $\,0.5478\,$ | $\,0.5517\,$ | $\,0.5557\,$ |
| $\,0.2\,$ | $\,0.5871\,$ | $\,0.5910\,$ | $\,0.5948\,$ |

*Hint: Note that the interval $-18<X<10$ is symmetric about the mean $\mu =-4.$*
worked_solution:
First, note that the given interval is symmetric about the mean:

$$
P(-18<X<10)=P(-4-14<X<-4+14)
$$

So, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-18<X<10) & =0.1113 \\ 2P(-4<X<10) & =0.1113 \\ P(-4<X<10) & =0.0557 \\ P(X<10)-P(X<-4) & =0.0557 \\ P(X<10)-0.5 & =0.0557 \\ P(X<10) & =0.5557 \\ P(X\le 10) & =0.5557\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 10) & =0.5557 \\ P(Z\le \frac{10-(-4)}{\sigma }) & =0.5557 \\ Φ(\frac{14}{\sigma }) & =0.5557 \\ \frac{14}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.5557)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.14)=0.5557\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.5557)=0.14.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{14}{\sigma } & =0.14 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{14}{0.14} \\ \sigma  & =100.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

First, note that the given interval is symmetric about the mean: P(−18<X<10)=P(−4−14<X<−4+14)

So, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

P(−18<X<10)=0.11132P(−4<X<10)=0.1113P(−4<X<10)=0.0557P(X<10)−P(X<−4)=0.0557P(X<10)−0.5=0.0557P(X<10)=0.5557P(X≤10)=0.5557

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by z-scoring:

P(X≤10)=0.5557P(Z≤10−(−4)σ)=0.5557Φ(14σ)=0.555714σ=Φ−1(0.5557)

According to the table, we have

Φ(0.14)=0.5557⇒Φ−1(0.5557)=0.14.

Therefore, we have

14σ=0.14σ=140.14σ=100.
